samples.summary: The two new Error Matrix rows contradict the rows and prose they sit next to instead of reconciling them. Immediately below, `Backend 5xx or network | 2 | SYSTEM` and above, `Backend 401/403 | 2 | UNAUTHORIZED`; §8.1 (cli.md:780-782) and packages/cli/README.md:127-128 both state `2` = system error (network, auth). The behaviour this delta generalises to *every* backend command is exit `1` with `HTTP_ERROR` (or a verbatim envelope) for 401/403/5xx alike — `forwardUpstreamError`/`outputError` only ever set `process.exitCode = 1` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:62,175). Since the PR is the change that makes this the universal path and it edits the very table that records the contract, the stale exit-2 rows should have been folded in or removed; as it stands the canonical design doc describes two mutually exclusive behaviours for the same HTTP responses and an agent branching on exit code (which the doc explicitly invites) gets it wrong.

samples.summary: Spec says a backend 401/403 reports code `UNAUTHORIZED`; the code path this delta makes universal never emits it. The HTTP client synthesises `{error:{code:'SESSION_EXPIRED'}}` (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:156-164) and `forwardUpstreamError` forwards it verbatim; a 403 or a 401 whose body is a Nest default becomes `HTTP_ERROR`. The delta's own formatter comment and new matrix row bless `SESSION_EXPIRED` as the 401 code without retiring the `UNAUTHORIZED` row, leaving the documented code an agent is told to branch on unimplemented.

samples.summary: The new doc comment overclaims: "Every command that talks to the backend routes its `!res.ok` branch through here" (and README.md:123-125 "Every command reports the same code for that condition"). `wafflebase login` still hits `/auth/token`, `/auth/me` and `/workspaces` and reports failures as bare non-JSON text plus `process.exit(1)` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:62-101, including a hand-rolled `HTTP ${wsRes.status}` string at line 98). Either bring login onto the shared envelope or scope the claim to non-auth commands; an agent told "every command" will try to `JSON.parse` login's stderr.

`forwardUpstreamError` and `upstreamErrorJson` are now two implementations of one rule, and the delta's comment even asserts they must produce "the same output for the same input" — a duplication the repo's reuse convention would rather see collapsed (e.g. `forwardUpstreamError` printing `upstreamErrorJson(res)` for the envelope case and throwing only for the non-envelope one, or a single classifier both call). Keeping two hand-synchronised copies of the classification is what lets them drift, and this delta widens the number of call sites depending on them staying identical.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location verified verbatim. docs/design/cli.md:1038 is `Backend 401/403 | 2 | UNAUTHORIZED`, :1041 is `Backend 5xx or network | 2 | SYSTEM`, and the two rows between them (:1039-1040) assert exit `1` with a forwarded envelope or `HTTP_ERROR` for backend error bodies — mutually exclusive contracts for the same HTTP responses in the same table. §8.1 (cli.md:780-782) and packages/cli/README.md:127-128 both still state `2` = system error (network, auth) and explicitly invite agents to branch on the exit code. The code matches the reviewer's account of the generalised path: forwardUpstreamError sets process.exitCode = 1 (formatter.ts:175) for envelope bodies and otherwise throws UpstreamHttpError (code `HTTP_ERROR`, formatter.ts:137-146,178) with no status-based branching; outputError sets exitCode = 1 unconditionally (formatter.ts:62). A grep of packages/cli/src for exitCode/process.exit found no site that ever sets 2 and no UNAUTHORIZED/SYSTEM code, so the exit-2 rows describe behaviour that does not exist anywhere. No guard reconciles them; the canonical design doc that records the contract was edited without folding in or removing the stale rows. This is design-doc discipline (a contract-bearing canonical doc left internally contradictory), squarely in the design-fit lane rather than the correctness lens.

finding.summary: Content/export paths now report `HTTP_ERROR`, not the `ERROR` code the task's acceptance criteria specify
finding.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:44-47 states the acceptance criterion: "An Express-shaped 404 body reaches stderr as {\"error\":{\"code\":\"ERROR\",\"message\":\"HTTP 404\"}} on the content/export paths and {\"error\":{\"code\":\"HTTP_ERROR\",...}} on the import/upload/download paths". The implementation instead defines `UpstreamHttpError { readonly code = 'HTTP_ERROR' }` so `outputError` emits `HTTP_ERROR` on the content/export paths too, and the new test (packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:219) asserts the new behaviour. Unifying the code may well be the better contract, but the acceptance criterion and the todo doc were not updated to record the deviation, so the documented spec and shipped behaviour now disagree.

verdict.reason: The finding misquotes the spec. The todo doc's Acceptance criteria (todo.md:55-60) require exactly the opposite of what the finding claims: an Express-shaped 404 must surface as {"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404: <upstream message>"}} with "the **same** code on every path (content/export as well as import/upload/download)". The lines the finding cites (44-47) are a Plan checkbox about the import/upload/download paths and also say HTTP_ERROR; a grep for any `"code":"ERROR"` spelling under docs/ returns no matches. The implementation conforms: UpstreamHttpError.code = 'HTTP_ERROR' (formatter.ts:137-146) matches upstreamErrorJson (formatter.ts:193-203), with 'ERROR' left only as the fallback for local/untyped failures (formatter.ts:41-47). The docs also record this, satisfying the fourth acceptance bullet (todo.md:66-67): packages/cli/README.md:116-126 documents HTTP_ERROR for non-envelope upstream bodies and notes every command reports the same code, and docs/design/cli.md:1040's error matrix row lists HTTP_ERROR. The cited test line (upstream-error.test.ts:219-221) is a comment describing the OLD flattening to {code:"ERROR"} that the change fixed; the assertions at :248-256 expect HTTP_ERROR on content/export as the criterion requires. So there is no documented-spec-vs-shipped-behaviour disagreement.

finding.summary: New `HTTP_ERROR` code on content/export paths contradicts the documented error-code contract in README/design doc, which the diff does not update
finding.evidence: packages/cli/README.md:116-120 documents "Typed errors (e.g., INVALID_DOCX, TYPE_MISMATCH, CONFIRMATION_REQ) carry a command-specific code agents can branch on; everything else reports \"ERROR\"". After this change `docs/slides/notes content|export` emit `HTTP_ERROR` (and a `HTTP <status>: <detail>` message) for every non-envelope failure, a new code that agents may branch on. Neither README nor docs/design/cli.md §10's Error Matrix (docs/design/cli.md:1024-1042, which maps backend 5xx/401/403 to exit 2 with codes SYSTEM/UNAUTHORIZED, not exit 1 / HTTP_ERROR) is touched by the diff; the corresponding skill files for content/export also list no HTTP_ERROR.

verdict.reason: The documentation the finding says is missing/untouched exists in the working tree. packages/cli/README.md:116-126 explicitly documents the new code: a failed request whose body is not the envelope "reports \"HTTP_ERROR\" with \"HTTP <status>\" — plus the upstream's own wording", and adds "Every command reports the same code for that condition, so the branch does not depend on which subcommand ran", reserving "ERROR" for local failures only. The reviewer's quote ("everything else reports ERROR") is a truncated excerpt that drops these sentences. docs/design/cli.md:1040 has a dedicated Error Matrix row in §10: "Backend error body is not the envelope | 1 | HTTP_ERROR | \"HTTP <status>\" (+ \": <upstream message>\" when the body had one)", distinct from the 401/403 (exit 2 UNAUTHORIZED, :1038) and 5xx/network (exit 2 SYSTEM, :1041) rows — so the matrix does not, as claimed, map this case to exit 2. Implementation matches the documented contract (formatter.ts:137-146, 173-179, 193-203: exit 1, code HTTP_ERROR, same output on both paths). docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-lessons.md:31-35 describes the undocumented state as the "first pass", i.e. already remedied. The only surviving fragment — content/export skill files not re-listing HTTP_ERROR — is minor doc-completeness, since the README states the code is uniform across commands so per-skill enumeration is not required; it fails no acceptance criterion and does not block.

finding.summary: Visual-harness change downgrades the font-readiness gate to a warning, the opposite of the posture its own task doc states, and the doc is not updated
finding.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:52-56 ("Notes") justifies the fix on the basis that "The check() wait already hard-fails (10s timeout) if a family never becomes available, so pulling Inter into the same set keeps the existing risk posture: an unreachable fonts.googleapis.com now reports a clear timeout instead of an opaque pixel diff." The diff introduces `settle()` (formatter of warnings) and wraps both the `fonts.check()` poll and the catch-all poll in it, so an unloaded font now yields exactly the opaque pixel diff the task says it is replacing. The plan checklist (lines 44-47) contains no item for making the wait best-effort, and the todo doc is not amended in this diff.

verdict.reason: Both halves of the finding are contradicted by the working tree. (1) The quoted doc text ("The check() wait already hard-fails ... keeps the existing risk posture: an unreachable fonts.googleapis.com now reports a clear timeout instead of an opaque pixel diff") does not exist. The Notes section at docs/tasks/active/20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:52-65 is titled "Risk posture — deliberately *not* hard-fail" and explicitly labels that hard-fail reasoning "an earlier draft of this plan" that "does not survive widening the set to the index.html families", because a fatal wait would turn a fonts.googleapis.com outage into a total harness failure across all ~200 captures; it states both waits therefore go through settle(), which warns naming the unsettled families and shoots anyway, accepting the baseline diff as the residual signal. (2) The plan checklist is not missing the item: lines 48-49 read "- [x] Downgrade both settling waits from hard-fail to warn-and-shoot (settle()), for the reason in Notes below." The implementation matches the doc: settle() wraps both waits (verify-visual-browser.mjs:395, :421), only timeouts are downgraded while other errors rethrow (:436-444), the describe callback names pending families (:406-419), and the in-file comments (:340-342, :388-394) carry the same rationale. There is no doc/code divergence and no unamended doc, so the design-fit defect as described (a change silently contradicting its own task doc's stated posture) is not present.

finding.summary: Unrelated scope creep: a frontend visual-harness font-waiting rewrite is bundled into a CLI error-envelope change
finding.evidence: The diff's stated subject is the CLI upstream-error forwarding helpers (`forwardUpstreamError` / `upstreamErrorJson` in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts) applied across docs/notes/slides/files. The hunk in packages/frontend/scripts/verify-visual-browser.mjs is a wholly separate concern: it expands VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES with Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono, adds a VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS matrix, adds a catch-all `status !== 'loading'` poll, and relocates `waitForFontsReady(page)` from before the harness-root wait to after the section-ready wait (capturePass). It shares no module, no test, and no acceptance criterion with the CLI work, and it materially changes when screenshots are taken in the visual-baseline lane (a change that can shift/invalidate the ~220 pinned baselines described in docs/design/harness-engineering.md). It should be its own change so it can be reviewed and baselined independently.

verdict.reason: Every factual element of the finding checks out in the working tree. verify-visual-browser.mjs:350-360 expands VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES with Inter, Fraunces, JetBrains Mono; :366 adds VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS = [400,500,600,700]; :421-428 adds the catch-all face.status !== "loading" poll; and capturePass calls waitForFontsReady(page) at :479, i.e. AFTER the harness-root wait (:467-468) and the section-ready loop (:470-474), materially changing when screenshots are taken. The delta's actual subject is the CLI error envelope: docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md states outcome/acceptance entirely in terms of forwardUpstreamError/upstreamErrorJson in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts, and the sibling review summaries describe the delta as the CLI !res.ok conversion only. No acceptance criterion or non-goal in that issue covers the visual harness; the harness work carries its own separate task file whose "Why this rides on the CLI branch" section (:70-76) explicitly concedes "This is unrelated to that branch's subject, and would normally be its own PR." The baseline-risk framing is grounded too: docs/design/harness-engineering.md:2403 records the lane as owning 220 baselines with Docker font pinning. This is unrequested scope creep, explicitly in this lens's lane, bundled into an unrelated change. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, reachable on every capture pass (capturePass is the sole screenshot path), and the CI-unblock rationale in the task doc explains the coupling rather than showing it absent.
